proposals.before: In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wencheng at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling, winning five battles in a single month, and was appointed brigade general of Shaan'an Garrison.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wenjin at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling, winning five battles in a single month, and was appointed brigade general of Shaan'an Garrison.
proposals.reason: Chinese 黃文金 is Huang Wenjin (given name 文金), not Wencheng.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wencheng at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling — five victories in one month — and was appointed brigade general of the Shaan'an Garrison.

proposals.before: He then joined Lei Zhengwan on converging routes against Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuanna in the field, captured the city, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
proposals.after: He then joined Lei Zhengwan on converging routes against Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuan, Nesan, and others in the field, captured the city, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
proposals.reason: Chinese 木仲沅訥三等 lists at least two names (木仲沅 and 訥三) plus others; English fused them into Mu Zhongyuanna.

proposals.before: He then joined Zhengwan on separate routes to invest Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuanna and others in battle, took the city, and was awarded a yellow jacket.
proposals.after: He then joined Zhengwan on separate routes to invest Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuan, Nesan, and others in battle, took the city, and was awarded a yellow jacket.
proposals.reason: Chinese 木仲沅訥三等 is a plural list of rebel chiefs, not one fused name.

proposals.before: Shi Dakai broke out from Baoding into Guangxi, seized Xing'an, dispatched followers to attack Guilin, and personally led his fiercest troops to camp on the Darong River.
proposals.after: Shi Dakai broke out from Baoqing into Guangxi, seized Xing'an, dispatched followers to attack Guilin, and personally led his fiercest troops to camp on the Darong River.
proposals.reason: Chinese 寶慶 is Baoqing (Hunan), not Baoding (保定).

proposals.before: Shi Dakai fled from Baoding into Guangxi, took Xing'an, sent partisans to attack Guilin, and himself led fierce rebels to encamp at Darong River.
proposals.after: Shi Dakai fled from Baoqing into Guangxi, took Xing'an, sent partisans to attack Guilin, and himself led fierce rebels to encamp at Darong River.
proposals.reason: Chinese 寶慶 is Baoqing, not Baoding.

proposals.before: The bandit chief Cao Shenzhang fled to Baliuping. A combined assault overthrew him, Canzhang was taken, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
proposals.after: The bandit chief Cao Canzhang fled to Baliuping. A combined assault overthrew him, Canzhang was taken, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
proposals.reason: Chinese 曹燦章 is Cao Canzhang (燦 can); English Shenzhang misreads the given name.

proposals.after: The bandit chief Cao Canzhang fled to hold Baliuping; a converging attack broke him, Canzhang was captured, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
